content:
lara: Quick sync — consolidating roadmap for inference-efficiency features (batching, prefix caching, quant profiles, eval-triggered alerts). Need final priorities for Q2 planning. Proposed slices: 1) lightweight advisor for per-route recommendations, 2) adaptive batching policy, 3) KV/prefix cache infra + simple API, 4) quant fallback + profiles, 5) eval-triggered alerting pipeline. Thoughts?
ajay: +1 on advisor early — highest customer ROI, but cache infra is blocking. Customers see huge variance without prefix cache.
tessa: Ops POV: adaptive batching needs capacity signals & safety nets. If we accelerate it we need rollout gates (p99 latency, error rate).
nick: For quant profiles we can ship two tiers: safe (8-bit) and aggressive (4-bit) with guardrails. Need eval-backfill to measure quality delta.
marta: Customer asks: FinServ & Health prioritized deterministic latency SLOs; they prefer cache + dedicated capacity over quant. We should map features to customer personas.
lara: Proposed ordering v1: M1 = KV cache + API + observability (blocking); M2 = advisor pilot + offline recommendations; M3 = adaptive batching + rollout DSL; M4 = quant profile beta w/ eval hooks; M5 = eval-triggered alerts in Console. M1 is a hard dependency for several asks.
ajay: Timeline check — M1 needs cached key schema, eviction policy, telemetry. Estimate 3 sprints infra + 1 API. Can we trim non-blocking telemetry from MVP?
tessa: MVP telemetry: per-route hit-rate + cache effectiveness metric. Token-level tracing can wait.
nick: Quant beta: reduce risk with automatic fallback to full-precision model on quality regression. That requires fast detect in eval pipeline.
marta: Also customers will expect enterprise toggles and slow-roll by tenant. Add opt-out + rollout controls to gates.
lara: Launch criteria suggestions per slice: M1: cache hit-rate > 30% on internal sims, no perf regressions p99, API auth + docs. M2: advisor recs hit NPS >= 4/5 in 3 pilot customers. M3: adaptive batching keeps p99 within 10% of baseline during rollout. M4: quant mean quality delta < 1% on key evals + safe fallback. M5: alerts surface within 5m of eval policy breach and include root-cause pointers.
ajay: Migration plan: provide migration helpers for cacheless workloads; telemetry opt-in for early adopters.
tessa: Rollout DSL suggestion: per-customer policy with max_batch_size, max_latency_ms, cost_target. Ops override allowed.
lara: Good. Action items: ajay - draft cache API + eviction proposal by EOD Fri; tessa - define rollout gates and DSL prototype by next Tue; nick - outline quant profile experiment + fallback mechanics by next Wed; marta - recruit top 5 pilot customers by end of week. Reconvene Thurs 11am PT. :calendar: 
infra-bot: Deployment window for cluster-3 maintenance Thu 02:00-04:00 UTC (FYI for rollouts).
marta: Compliance note from Health customer: KMS for cached keys required — mark for Private deployments.
lara: KMS integration = must-have for Private, optional for Hosted GA.
ajay: Risk: encrypted cache keys complicate eviction/rehydration. I'll sync with security.
tessa: Eval-triggered alerts need signal taxonomy defined (concordance, hallucination rate, latency drift). Add to product grooming.
lara: Will add to grooming board. Thanks all — see you Thurs. :thumbsup:
